extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical geometry (Euclid), mathematics students and teachers
extracted.subtask_description: A sequence of classical geometric propositions and constructions from Euclid's Elements (Books I and II), including theorems about triangles, parallelograms, squares, the Pythagorean theorem and algebraic-geometric identities (rectangles and gnomons).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXVII: Triangles on same base and between same parallels are equal
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the triangles ABC, DBC be upon the same base BC and between the same parallels AD, BC: the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DBC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: produce AD both ways to points E, F; draw through B and C lines parallel to CA and BD to form parallelograms EBCA and DBCF. Each triangle is half its corresponding parallelogram because the diameter bisects it; halves of equal things are equal. (Proof shows forming parallelograms and comparing halves.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXVIII: Triangles on equal bases and between same parallels are equal
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the triangles ABC, DEF be upon equal bases BC, EF, and between the same parallels BF, AD: the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DEF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: produce AD to G,H and draw parallels from B and F to form parallelograms GBCA and DEFH which lie on equal bases and between the same parallels; each triangle is half its parallelogram because the diameter bisects it; halves of equal things are equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XXXIX: Equal triangles on same base and same side are between same parallels
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the equal triangles ABC, DBC be upon the same base BC, and upon the same side of it; they are between the same parallels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: join AD. If AD were not parallel to BC, draw AE through A parallel to BC; triangle ABC would equal EBC (same base and parallels) which contradicts equality relations. Hence AD is parallel to BC; therefore triangles are between the same parallels.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XL: Equal triangles on equal bases in same line and towards same parts are between same parallels
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the equal triangles ABC, DEF be upon equal bases BC, EF, in the same straight line BF, and towards the same parts; they are between the same parallels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Join AD; assume AD not parallel to BF and derive a contradiction by drawing AG parallel to BF and comparing triangles on equal bases between the same parallels; conclude AD must be parallel to BF.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLI: Parallelogram on same base and between same parallels is double the triangle
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram and triangle be upon the same base, and between the same parallels; the parallelogram shall be double of the triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let parallelogram ABCD and triangle EBC be on same base BC and between the same parallels BC, AE. Join AC; triangle ABC equals triangle EBC (same base and parallels). The parallelogram ABCD is double triangle ABC because the diagonal divides it into two equal triangles; hence parallelogram is double triangle EBC.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLII (Problem): Construct parallelogram equal to a given triangle with given angle
rubrics_metrics.description: To describe a parallelogram that shall be equal to a given triangle, and have one of its angles equal to a given rectilineal angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: bisect BC, build angle at midpoint equal to given angle, draw parallels through A and C to form parallelogram FECG. Show FECG equals triangle ABC because triangles on equal bases and between same parallels lead to parallelogram being double the half-triangle, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLIII: Complements about the diameter of a parallelogram are equal
rubrics_metrics.description: The complements of the parallelograms which are about the diameter of any parallelogram, are equal to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let ABCD be parallelogram with diagonal AC and EH, FG parallelograms about AC; BK, KD are complements making the whole ABCD. Show equality by pairing equal triangles (diagonal bisects parallelogram) and comparing sums to deduce BK equals KD.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLIV (Problem): Apply parallelogram equal to given triangle to a given straight line with given angle
rubrics_metrics.description: To a given straight line to apply a parallelogram, which shall be equal to a given triangle, and have one of its angles equal to a given rectilineal angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: form parallelogram BEFG equal to triangle C with angle EBG equal to given angle D, align BE with AB, extend and complete parallelogram; use properties of parallel lines and intersections to get required parallelogram LB equal to triangle C and angle ABM equal to D.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLV (Problem): Parallelogram equal to a rectilineal figure with a given angle
rubrics_metrics.description: To describe a parallelogram equal to a given rectilineal figure, and having an angle equal to a given rectilineal angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decompose given figure into triangles (join diagonal), construct parallelograms equal to those triangles with the given angle, join them to form the required parallelogram. Corollary: explains how to apply such a parallelogram to a given straight line.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLVI (Problem): Describe a square on a given straight line
rubrics_metrics.description: To describe a square upon a given straight line AB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: at A draw AC at right angles to AB, make AD equal to AB, draw parallels through D and B to form ADEB parallelogram; show all sides equal and all angles right, hence ADEB is a square. Corollary: any parallelogram with one right angle has all right angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLVII (Theorem - Pythagoras): Square on hypotenuse equals squares on other sides
rubrics_metrics.description: In any right-angled triangle, the square which is described upon the side subtending the right angle is equal to the squares described upon the sides which contain the right angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct squares on each side; draw parallels and join segments to form equal parallelograms and triangles; show the square on the hypotenuse equals sum of the two squares on the legs by decomposing into equal parallelograms (uses previous propositions about parallelograms being double triangles).

rubrics_metrics.name: PROP. XLVIII (Converse of Pythagoras): If square on one side equals squares on other two, angle is right
rubrics_metrics.description: If the square described upon one of the sides of a triangle be equal to the squares described upon the other two sides of it; the angle contained by these two sides is a right angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: from A draw AD at right angles to AC and make AD equal to AB; compare squares and apply equality of triangles and sides to deduce angle BAC equals right angle DAC, hence BAC is right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II Definition I: Right-angled parallelogram
rubrics_metrics.description: Every right angled parallelogram is said to be contained by any two of the straight lines which contain one of the right angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition only; terminological: identifies what is meant by a parallelogram 'contained by' two lines when it has a right angle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II Definition II: Gnomon
rubrics_metrics.description: In every parallelogram, any of the parallelograms about a diameter, together with the two complements, is called a gnomon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the gnomon construction and notation (e.g., the parallelogram HG together with complements AF, FC is the gnomon, abbreviated by letters at opposite angles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. I: Rectangle decomposition across parts
rubrics_metrics.description: If there be two straight lines, one of which is divided into any number of parts; the rectangle contained by the two straight lines, is equal to the rectangles contained by the undivided line and the several parts of the divided line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: erect a rectangle equal to one line and draw parallels through division points to partition the large rectangle into subrectangles equal to the rectangles with the parts; formal geometric algebraic identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. II: Sum of rectangles equals square
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be divided into any two parts, the rectangles contained by the whole and each of the parts are together equal to the square of the whole line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct square on whole line and parallels through division point to produce two rectangles whose areas equal the rectangles AB·AC and AB·BC; sum equals square of AB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. III: Rectangle of whole and part equals rectangle of parts plus square of part
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be divided into any two parts, the rectangle AB, BC is equal to the rectangle AC, CB, together with the square of BC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct square on the part and use parallels to partition and compare areas; geometric representation of (a)(b) = (a - b)(b) + b^2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. IV: Square of whole equals sum of squares plus twice rectangle
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Straight line be divided into any two parts, the square of the whole line is equal to the squares of the two parts, together with twice the rectangle contained by the parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric demonstration decomposes square on whole into two squares on parts plus two equal rectangles (gnomons), yielding algebraic identity (a+b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 + 2ab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. V: Rectangle of unequal parts plus square between sections equals square of half
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be divided into two equal parts, and also into two unequal parts; the rectangle contained by the unequal parts, together with the square of the line between the points of section, is equal to the square of half the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct square on half-line and appropriate parallels/gnomons to show area relationships; yields identity related to (difference of squares) and decomposition into gnomon plus square.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. VI: Bisected line produced — area identity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be bisected, and produced to any point, the rectangle contained by the whole line thus produced, and the part of it produced, together with the square of half the line bisected, is equal to the square of the straight line which is made up of the half and the part produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric area construction using squares and gnomons; corresponds to algebraic identity relating (half + extra)^2 to products involving the extended line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. VII: Squares relation with twice rectangle
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be divided into any two parts, the squares of the whole line, and of one of the parts, are equal to twice the rectangle contained by the whole and that part, together with the square of the other part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric proof using previously constructed gnomons and squares; algebraic form relates a^2 + b^2 to 2ab + c^2 in the given decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. VIII: Four times rectangle plus square equals square of sum
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be divided into any two parts, four times the rectangle contained by the whole line, and one of the parts, together with the square of the other part, is equal to the square of the straight line which is made up of the whole and that part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct auxiliary equal segments and squares; use symmetry and complements to show four equal rectangles sum to quadruple of one rectangle and combine with squares to form the square of combined length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. IX: Squares of unequal parts relate to halves and sections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be divided into two equal, and also into two unequal parts; the squares of the two unequal parts are together double of the squares of the half the line, and of the line between the points of section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric construction using perpendiculars and equalities to derive that sum of squares of AD and DB equals twice (AC^2 + CD^2); corresponds to decompositions of sums of squares in terms of midpoints and offsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book II PROP. X: Squares of produced line and produced part double relation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a straight line be bisected, and produced to any point, the square of the whole line thus produced, and the square of the part of it produced, are together double of the square of half the line bisected, and of the square of the line made up of the half and the part produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from preceding propositions; establishes a double-square relation for the produced line and the produced part, proved by geometric decomposition into gnomons and squares.
